notes: Reported claim 150.042.N1: the page continues a discussion of composition and says that the Sigma data satisfying (3) amount to a category in M over I_M. The diagonal note calls the corresponding object ordered and identifies flag-indexed pieces with chains lying over flags of I. These are reported manuscript claims, not reader proofs.

Reported claim 150.042.N2: the diagonal note says that the displayed intersection condition can be verified at n=2 and interprets it as the order on Sigma(z) being induced from I(k). The literal small indices include commas omitted by both witnesses; the first right separator and the overtraced left ij remain doubtful. No mathematical normalization or proof of this equivalence was performed by reader_c.

Reported claim 150.042.N3: the main text proposes a stratified-space construction, says that it will not use the listed hypotheses in full, and retains a weaker embedding requirement with a hatted omitted index. The discussion of conical structures remains parenthetical, with no supplied stop after its closing parenthesis.

Reported claim 150.042.N4: the final paragraph chooses pairs of flags d subset d-prime with d not cofinal in d-prime, and states 2^n choices when d-prime is displayed with endpoints i_0 and i_n, with an uncertain horizontal mark at a crossing between them. The words ne and pas were read from their separate letter strokes. The expression de longueur n is live; the long curve above it attaches the raised tuple and does not cancel the phrase.

Checked observation 150.042.N5, performed by root: for an (n+1)-element chain with specified maximum m, the subsets excluding m correspond to all subsets of the other n elements, and adjoining m gives a bijection to the subsets containing m. Both families therefore have 2^n members when the empty subset is included in the excluding family. The page does not state an empty-flag convention here. This conditional counting observation does not resolve the literal negation and is not a verification of the author’s whole construction or count under an unstated flag convention.

The manuscript preserves unconventional punctuation after axiome and équivaut as colons. The compressed main est/et and the punctuation at the right edge after manifestement remain unresolved; no grammar repair was used. The latter can leave an apparent extra parenthesis, and that possibility is retained.

The star note rises diagonally through the left margin and crosses the main writing. Its cf. p. 15-prime reference is one source occurrence, not the additional main-line voir reference suggested by H. Main-line satisfaisant, par construction and Catégorie dans remain on the baseline.

There is one overtraced opening en group in the marginal note, not a separate canceled en followed by a second en. Both vertical diagram relations are literal pairs of upright strokes. The prose Sigma(z) has no star although the diagram Sigma_*(z) and set definition do.
The foliation 41 is thin and pale at the lower left; hand attribution is uncertain and it is not promoted to the author’s own mspage number. No independent author page number is visible at the head.

Method: one whole image and both native full-resolution halves were read once, with all main and marginal text, insertions and cancellations compared against C and H. Thirty-three crop images were generated and all viewed. The three overlapping diagonal-note crops were necessary for readable note orientation. One additional small-formula detail was taken for an unsettled index group. The au_dessus_main crop first landed on the continuation line; au_dessus_completion is the single necessary completion, and both images were retained. Existing unsettled est_composition and manifestement crops were reopened, without regeneration. No OCR, external research, other page/readers’ returns or TeX compilation was used.

The first reader’s initial comma interpretation in the raised Sigma pair was explicitly corrected after distinguishing the first i’s detached dot and low body from the Sigma’s own terminal curl. The final reading has no comma and has j alone as the second index. Every change row cites its source crop; original C doubts inside canceled words remain unless independently readable letter by letter.

Root-discovered correction during final visual review: reader_c’s first return had silently normalized drawn continuation strokes as \ldots or \cdots. Existing margin_upper, margin_middle, weaker_map and dprime_tuple crops were reopened for that concrete issue; no new versions of those crops were generated. At root’s request, one new opening_index_count crop was made and viewed because no earlier tight crop included that full index. Ten ellipsis groups across seven formula/list places were corrected: the opening full Sigma index and both marginal full Sigma indices each have one long dash; the marginal x-chain and intersection continuation each have two short dashes; the prose flag has one long dash; the weaker display has two strokes in the left index and respectively one and two around the hatted target index; the raised tuple has a narrow uncertain dash at the crossing q stroke. Original witness quotations were preserved unchanged in the metadata.

Root’s final accounting refinement: the est/et word, manifestement comma/closing-parenthesis, marginal dash/arrow, and canceled de/et retain the witnesses’ readings as alternatives. Their records remain in doubts and audit boxes, but their four uncertainty-only rows were removed from the corrections list; they are not counted as witness errors.

Crop accounting: 33 physical crop images represent 32 cropped places. The retained au_dessus_main mistarget and its one necessary au_dessus_completion are counted as one place. Root has directly viewed all 33 images, including the additional opening_index_count crop and the existing crops reopened for literal continuation counts.
